_doc: Opt-in baseline for `node scripts/check-all.mjs --baseline scripts/check-all-baseline.json`. Lists the checks EXPECTED to fail on a partial container checkout because the DEPLOY build chain regenerates them (pure structural idempotency: 'would update N files/hashes'). With the baseline, check-all exits 0 on 'zero NEW regressions' and reds only on an UNEXPECTED fail — so a session/agent can trust the exit code instead of re-deriving 'which of the 25 are idem noise' by hand every time. The plain `check-all.mjs` (no flag) stays STRICT; THAT is the Cloudflare deploy gate — never weaken it. RULES: (1) only add a check here if it is a deploy-regenerated builder whose ONLY container-failure mode is 'output would be rebuilt' — NEVER a hard gate. The runner enforces this in two layers: (1a) POSITIVE — every entry must be an '(idem)'-labeled regeneration check (no hard gate is '(idem)'-tagged), which structurally excludes fabrications/honesty/locale-parity/no-fetch/etc.; (1b) a short DENYLIST backstop of the most critical hard gates by script name (NOT an exhaustive catalog). A non-'(idem)' or denylisted entry aborts with exit 2. Layers do not replace reviewer judgment — you still confirm each entry is genuinely deploy-regenerated. (2) Each entry carries a dated reason. (3) If a baselined check PASSES, the runner warns to prune it (keeps this list honest). Regenerate the set by running `node scripts/check-all.mjs`, confirming each red is a 'would update' regenerator, and copying its label here. NOT baselined on purpose (they flag SEMANTIC data drift, not idempotency, so they stay visible even though the cost-index-refresh workflow also heals them): 'Cost-index picker' (a stale dollarRef flag vs the seed) and 'Cost-index revisions sync' (published readings moved on the 07-13/07-15 reads).
